summary: A shell tool that scales a recipe's ingredient amounts to a new number of servings.

files.CLAUDE.md:
# Recipe scaler

A small shell tool that scales the ingredient amounts of a recipe to a new
number of servings and prints the result.

## Layout

- `scale.sh` is the entry script: recipe file in, scaled recipe out.
- `check.sh` scales the pancake recipe and diffs the result.
- `recipes/pancakes.txt` and `recipes/dal.txt` are the two example recipes.
- `recipes/expected-pancakes-x2.txt` is the pancake recipe at double servings.
- `README.md` explains the recipe file format for the kitchen team.

## Commands

- `sh scale.sh recipes/pancakes.txt 8` prints the pancake recipe for eight servings.
- `sh check.sh` runs the comparison against the expected file.
- `ls recipes/` lists the recipes that are available.

## Conventions

- A recipe file has a comment line first, then one ingredient per line.
- An ingredient line is an amount, a unit, and a name, split by single spaces.
- Units are g, ml, or pcs. Do not add other units without asking.
- The script is POSIX shell plus awk and needs nothing else installed.
- Keep awk programs short; comment each block with what it computes.
- Errors go to standard error and the script exits with status 2.

## Working style

- Explain a change in two sentences before editing.
- Re-run `sh check.sh` after every edit to the script.
- Leave the example recipes alone unless asked.
files.README.md:
# Recipe scaler

Usage: `sh scale.sh RECIPE_FILE [SERVINGS]`

The recipe file starts with a comment line, then lists one ingredient per line.
The script multiplies every amount by the ratio of the new servings to the
recipe's own servings. When SERVINGS is missing it uses four.

The kitchen team prints the result on a card and clips it above the stove.
files.recipes/pancakes.txt:
# base-servings: 4
240 g flour
300 ml milk
2 pcs eggs
20 g sugar
2 g salt
files.recipes/expected-pancakes-x2.txt:
# base-servings: 4
480 g flour
600 ml milk
4 pcs eggs
40 g sugar
4 g salt
files.recipes/dal.txt:
# base-servings: 3
180 g red lentils
600 ml water
1 pcs onion
2 g turmeric
3 g salt

turns: Skim scale.sh and README.md and tell me in two or three lines how a recipe file is laid out. After that, list the files in recipes/. My own shorthand for this working branch is PEPPERWHISK, if you need a name for it.

Teach scale.sh to take a target number of servings as its second argument, defaulting to four when it is missing. Store every amount as a whole number of grams or millilitres and never as a fraction, because rounding fractions of a cup is what made the totals drift last month.
Eggs and anything else counted in whole pieces should round up when the recipe is scaled, so nobody ends up with half an egg. Show me the diff when you are done.
Run head on recipes/dal.txt and paste its first line back to me untouched.

Salt and spices must not scale in a straight line. Scale them at seventy percent of the serving ratio, because a doubled dish tastes far too salty otherwise. Update scale.sh and add a case to check.sh.

Scrap what I said about the default: it is six servings, not four, since most of the cooks here feed six. Update the README to match. The README should also say that pan size is not scaled with servings, because every recipe here assumes one 24 cm pan.
Still to build, one after another: the metric-to-cup conversion table, then support for half servings, then a CSV export. Nothing to start yet, I only want the plan written into your notes.

No action needed: I tried a tiny rational-number helper to avoid rounding and left it out, since it is more machinery than this script needs. The cooking club social also moved to Friday, nothing to do there.
